findings.evidence: robots.txt blocks Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider, CCBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, GPTBot, meta-externalagent (a training-corpus crawler) but permits retrieval-time AI crawlers.

suggested_action.summary: This is frequently intentional and not necessarily a defect. It forgoes future parametric-memory coverage only; leave the decision with the site owner.

findings.title: Training-corpus crawler blocked, retrieval intact

limitations.reason: Actual agreement across the wider web about the brand's facts requires a search or web-scale index API. No free, deterministic, rate-safe source exists.
limitations.note: CHK-D-025/026/027 audit only the anchoring the site itself provides for that corroboration, not corroboration itself.

limitations.reason: Detecting a same-name collision with an unrelated entity requires a corpus of other entities.
limitations.note: CHK-D-027 covers only self-consistency, the site-side half.

limitations.reason: Live-querying a generative engine would break determinism, the 5-minute budget, and reproducibility.
limitations.note: This audit measures retrievability and correctness of what the site exposes, never observed citation outcomes.

limitations.reason: Field engagement outcomes (bounce, dwell, scroll, conversion, task success) are not observable read-only.
limitations.note: Reported not_determinable where the gap is itself actionable.

limitations.reason: llms.txt is not recommended as a substantive fix: a 137k-domain measurement found 97% of existing llms.txt files were never requested. This audit declines to recommend adding one on that evidence (D-007).
limitations.note: Stated here rather than omitted (D-014) — the officials' Q&A confirms recommending it is an acceptable position, so silence about it would look indistinguishable from having missed it.
